title: SnapFC ⚽️ - Built a tiny physics-based soccer game you can play in your browser
author: igcorrec
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I've been working on this small web game called SnapFC on the side and figured i'd finally share it here.

It's a simple turned-based soccer game where you drag and release to snap your players, a mix between tabletop and physics. Games are quick but there's some strategy once you get used to it.

I'm still polishing it so i'm mostly trying to understand if it feels good to play, is it clear what to do, does it stay fun after a few matches?

You can play against CPU and or play against a friend online.

Hit me up if you want to play with me online, and your quick thoughts would help a lot!

[https://snapfc.com](https://snapfc.com/)

comments.author: Vlaxilla
comments.body:
Hey man just tried your game.

I would say it was quite fun and its intuitive i played on mobile and couldn't get full power on the edges but still was good fun. 

After 1 match I think the novelty wears off tho but I can see it being very fun in multiplayer kinda reminds me of that billiards iPhone game you played with friends. So if you add tournaments and things to it online can be great.

It kinda reminded me of Microstars/Soccerstars bubbleheads I used to collect. It would be good if you can get some inspiration from it and make some characters different/better kinda like Ultimate team or at least collect skins. 

Anywaya its good bro keep at it 💪 i think with a few added things it can be a great game

replies.author: igcorrec
replies.body:
appreciate you taking the time to play and write this up!

That edge power thing is a good catch, it's a challenge i'm trying to solve for mobile. And yeah, fair point on the it wearing off, I’m starting to realize it needs more progression and reasons to keep ppl playing.

Glad you called out multiplayer too, i definitely want to lean into it more.

Really helpful feedback, thanks for this!

comments.author: VRSportz
comments.body: I will try later and feedback. I also make sports 2d games. Looks a bit like subbuteo which I played a lot as a kid

replies.author: igcorrec
replies.body: appreciate you taking the time to try it out later, love to hear your thoughts, esp since you’ve built sports games yourself. Any feedback would be super helpful!

comments.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
comments.body: Pretty fun but ironically the angle snapping of the contact point with the ball seems to limit shots a bit.

replies.author: igcorrec
replies.body: really helpful, can you clarify a bit, do you mean the angle feels like it locks in too much?

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body: Yeah, it feels like although I have fine control over the angle going into the ball it them seems like it snaps (perhaps to the polygons of the ball?) limiting my actual options for the ball trajectory.

replies.author: igcorrec
replies.body: i'll play around and adjust the accuracy, thanks for clarifying!
